summary: Establishes standards for office operations, facility maintenance, and workspace safety.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Workspace safety inspection checklist with completion records
Facility maintenance schedule and work order logs
Staff safety incident reports tied to office environment
Emergency exit plan and posted safety documentation
justification: Corridor row 1-021 'Patient & Staff Safety Program' (HH1-8A, HH1-8A.01) covers the physical safety environment for both patients and staff under the emergency preparedness and safety framework. OP-FM-001 governs office operations, facility maintenance, AND workspace safety — the safety component aligns with 1-021, but office operations (facility maintenance schedules, utility management, workspace standards) are purely administrative functions not addressed by the safety program row. PARTIAL with MEDIUM confidence: 1-021 is the structural parent for the workspace safety component; office and facility management governance is an administrative operational layer beyond the Corridor's safety program scope.

summary: Establishes standards for operating and overseeing branch offices or satellite locations.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Branch office authorization documentation and ACHC/licensing for each location
Organizational chart showing branch location reporting lines
Branch compliance monitoring records and supervisory visit logs
Satellite location policy attestations and oversight documentation
justification: Corridor row 1-001 'Organizational Structure' (HH1-1A, HH1-3A) requires that the agency's organizational structure be defined including accountability relationships. Branch offices and satellite locations are components of the organizational structure and must be incorporated into ACHC organizational documentation. PARTIAL because 1-001 requires the structure be documented — OP-FM-002 governs the specific operational standards for running and overseeing satellite locations, including compliance verification, local supervision, and location-specific policies, which exceed the structural documentation requirement.

summary: Defines standards for vendor selection, qualification, monitoring, and performance evaluation.
justification: No Corridor row in pages 7–31 governs general vendor selection, qualification, monitoring, and performance evaluation as an operational program. The Corridor's 2-033 (Business Associates) governs PHI contractual vendor controls — already mapped in the CO domain for BA management and in the IT domain for vendor security assessment. OP-FM-003 governs the broader vendor management lifecycle (supplier qualification, performance evaluation, contract management) for medical supply vendors, equipment vendors, and service vendors that are not PHI handlers. This is procurement governance in the Modern Operational Governance Layer.

summary: Establishes standards for handling agency mail, correspondence, and official communications.
justification: No Corridor row in pages 7–31 governs mail and correspondence handling as an administrative function. While HIPAA requires that PHI-containing correspondence be handled securely (covered by CO-HP-001 and CO-DC-001), mail and correspondence management as an operational standard — incoming mail routing, correspondence retention, official communication protocols — is purely administrative governance with no Corridor crosswalk equivalent.

summary: Establishes the agency's emergency preparedness, response, and business continuity plan per 42 CFR 484.102.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Written emergency operations plan with all required 42 CFR §484.102 elements
Annual emergency management exercise records with after-action reports
Business continuity plan with recovery time objectives
Emergency management committee meeting minutes and plan review records
justification: Corridor row 1-011 'Emergency Management' (HH1-8A, HH1-8A.01, HH1-8A.02, HH1-8B) explicitly implements the CMS Emergency Preparedness requirement (42 CFR §484.102) for home health agencies. OP-FM-005 is the enterprise emergency operations and business continuity plan — an exact match to the Corridor row. The policy explicitly cites 42 CFR §484.102, confirming direct regulatory alignment. Evidence: P, D, I, O. Note: EMERGENCY_MANAGEMENT_SEMANTIC_CLUSTER with OP-SL-006 and OP-SL-007 — all reference 1-011 as their regulatory parent.

summary: Establishes standards for referral receipt, screening, eligibility determination, and timely intake processing.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Referral source disclosure documentation and financial relationship attestations
Intake screening checklist with eligibility determination criteria
Referral-to-admission timeliness tracking records
Referral source communication logs
justification: Corridor row 1-004 'Referral Disclosure and Care Decisions' (HH1-2A.01, HH1-2A.02) covers the disclosure of referral sources and financial relationships, and non-steering provisions — the regulatory aspect of referral management. OP-IM-001 governs the full referral-to-intake workflow including receipt, screening, eligibility determination, and timeliness standards. PARTIAL because 1-004 covers the referral disclosure obligation precisely, but the operational intake workflow — screening criteria, intake processing timelines, eligibility verification procedures — is a clinical operations program beyond the disclosure row's scope.

summary: Defines clinical and operational criteria for patient acceptance including non-discrimination requirements and service capability assessment.
corridorPolicyTitle: Patient Access to Care; Patient Nondiscrimination and ADA
realEvidenceArtifacts: Patient acceptance criteria documentation with clinical capability assessment protocol
Non-discrimination policy acknowledgment and patient rights notice
Denial-of-service documentation with reason codes
ADA accommodation request records
justification: Corridor row 1-007 'Patient Access to Care' (HH1-1A, HH1-5B) covers patient access rights and non-discrimination in care access. Row 2-007 'Patient Nondiscrimination and ADA' (HH1-5B, HH1-5B.01) covers ADA compliance and non-discrimination requirements in service delivery. OP-IM-002 governs admission criteria including both the non-discrimination requirement (covered by 1-007 and 2-007) and the clinical service capability assessment (agency's ability to meet the specific patient's clinical needs). PARTIAL because the non-discrimination and access components align directly with the Corridor rows, but clinical service capability assessment criteria — determining whether the agency can safely and effectively serve a patient's specific clinical needs — is a clinical governance function beyond the Corridor rows' scope.

summary: Defines the agency's geographic service area boundaries and standards for ensuring coverage throughout the defined area.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Service area map with defined geographic boundaries
ACHC licensure documentation showing authorized service area
Coverage gap analysis documentation
Service area expansion/contraction notification records
justification: Corridor row 1-005 'Service Area/Community Health Needs' (HH1-1A) covers the definition and documentation of the agency's geographic service area — the primary content of OP-IM-003. The Corridor requires the agency to define its service area and demonstrate coverage capacity. OP-IM-003 governs service area boundary definition and coverage standards — an exact match to the service area component of 1-005. Note: the Corridor row's 'Community Health Needs' component extends beyond OP-IM-003's scope (geographic boundaries focus), but the primary service area definition element aligns directly. DIRECT for the primary regulatory obligation.

summary: Defines the process for receiving, investigating, and resolving patient complaints with documentation and trending requirements.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Complaint/grievance log with complaint type, date received, and resolution date
Complaint investigation records with root cause documentation
Complaint trending report with corrective action records
Patient notification of complaint resolution documentation
justification: Corridor row 1-023 'Complaint Management' (HH1-6A) implements 42 CFR §484.110(e) which requires home health agencies to have a process for receiving, investigating, and resolving patient complaints. OP-PA-001 governs the complaint and grievance resolution process — an exact match to the Corridor row. Evidence: P, D, I.

summary: Establishes standards for verifying patient identity at each visit to prevent service delivery errors.
justification: No Corridor row in pages 7–31 specifically governs patient identification and verification at the point of care (visit-level identity verification to prevent service delivery errors). While HIPAA requires patient identity verification for PHI access (mapped in the CO domain) and patient rights require that patients be treated with dignity and accuracy, the operational patient ID verification protocol at each home visit — confirming the correct patient before service delivery — is a patient safety program without a specific Corridor crosswalk row. Modern patient safety governance concept.

summary: Defines standards for providing language access services to patients with limited English proficiency.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Interpreter services policy with qualified interpreter standards
Language access service records by patient and visit type
Qualified medical interpreter credential documentation
Dual-language or translated patient materials inventory
justification: Corridor row 2-031 'Interpreter Services' (HH2-3A.01) directly governs the provision of interpreter services for patients with limited English proficiency — an exact match to OP-PA-003's scope. The Corridor requires that language access services be available and that qualified interpreters are used. OP-PA-003 operationalizes this exact requirement. Evidence: P, D, I.

summary: Establishes standards for culturally sensitive and respectful service delivery across diverse patient populations.
corridorPolicyTitle: Interpreter Services; Patient Nondiscrimination and ADA
realEvidenceArtifacts: Cultural competency training completion records for all clinical staff
Patient population demographic assessment and service gap analysis
Culturally adapted care plan documentation
Community cultural liaison partnerships and referral records
justification: Corridor row 2-031 'Interpreter Services' (HH2-3A.01) covers language access as a component of culturally competent care. Row 2-007 'Patient Nondiscrimination and ADA' (HH1-5B, HH1-5B.01) establishes non-discrimination in service delivery across protected characteristics including national origin and ethnicity. OP-PA-004 governs cultural competency broadly — training, culturally adapted care approaches, and equitable service delivery. PARTIAL because the language access and non-discrimination components align with the Corridor rows, but a formal cultural competency program (clinical staff training, culturally adapted care plans, community liaison partnerships) extends beyond the interpreter services and non-discrimination rows' scope. Note: cross-domain overlap with HR training domain for workforce cultural competency education.

summary: Establishes protocols for respecting and safeguarding patient property during home health visits.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Patient rights notice covering property respect and privacy
Property damage incident reports with resolution documentation
Staff training records on patient property protocols
Patient acknowledgment of rights including property protections
justification: Corridor row 2-006 'Patient Rights and Responsibilities' (HH1-5A, HH1-5A.01) implements 42 CFR §484.50, which establishes the patient's rights to privacy and dignity — implicitly covering respect for patient property in the home setting. OP-PA-005 operationalizes the property protection component of patient rights into specific visit protocols. PARTIAL with MEDIUM confidence because the patient rights row establishes the obligation to respect patient property, but the specific visit protocols — documenting the patient's environment at each visit, handling personal items, reporting property concerns — are operational governance beyond the rights notification row's scope.

summary: Defines scheduling standards including timeliness, frequency compliance, and patient notification requirements.
justification: No Corridor row in pages 7–31 governs visit scheduling management as an operational program. While visit frequency requirements are embedded in clinical protocol rows (e.g., nursing visit frequencies under CoP), scheduling workflow governance — timeliness standards, frequency compliance monitoring, patient notification of scheduling changes, visit confirmation protocols — is an operational workflow management function without a Corridor crosswalk equivalent. Forcing this to any clinical protocol row would collapse scheduling operations governance into clinical service delivery, a categorical error.

summary: Establishes 24/7 availability requirements, on-call staffing, and after-hours clinical response protocols per CMS CoP.
realEvidenceArtifacts: On-call staffing schedule with qualified clinical coverage documentation
After-hours call log with response time and clinical action records
On-call protocol documentation including triage criteria and escalation procedures
24/7 availability attestation and contact directory
justification: Support strengthened to Corridor Section 4 row 15 (On-Call/Weekend Staffing). Existing OP-SL-002 policy content, triage protocol, and after-hours call logs directly support this row. This is a row-normalization fix to existing policy support, not a new mapping expansion.

summary: Establishes standards for staff vehicle use, mileage documentation, insurance requirements, and transportation safety.
justification: No Corridor row in pages 7–31 governs staff vehicle use, mileage documentation, auto insurance requirements, or transportation safety. Vehicle and driver safety is an operational risk management governance function — covered in some organizations under OSHA general duty or risk management policy, but without a home health ACHC or CoP crosswalk row. Note: operational overlap with RM domain risk management governance, but RM did not tag transportation safety to a specific Corridor row either.

summary: Defines procedures for procurement, maintenance, calibration, and replacement of medical equipment and supplies.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Medical equipment inventory with calibration and maintenance records
Equipment procurement standards and qualification criteria
Equipment failure and replacement documentation
Biohazardous supply disposal records
justification: Corridor row 1-013 'Hazardous Material and Waste Management' (HH1-8A) covers the management of hazardous materials and waste in the clinical setting — the closest Corridor row touching medical supplies governance (specifically the handling and disposal of medical supplies that involve infection risk or hazardous materials). OP-SL-004 governs the full medical equipment and supply management lifecycle: procurement, maintenance, calibration, and replacement. PARTIAL with MEDIUM confidence: the hazardous material row covers the disposal/handling element precisely, but equipment calibration, preventive maintenance programs, procurement standards, and replacement criteria are clinical operational governance beyond the Corridor's waste management row. A dedicated equipment management row may exist in Section 4 of the Corridor that was not confirmed from the pages 7–31 reading relevant to this domain.

summary: Defines requirements for communication systems supporting clinical operations including EMR, telephony, and secure messaging.
corridorPolicyTitle: Interface of Patient Data and Management Systems; Fostering Internal Communication
realEvidenceArtifacts: EMR system governance documentation with clinical communication requirements
Secure messaging policy with encryption and PHI handling requirements
After-hours communication system availability documentation
Internal communication standards and staff acknowledgment records
justification: Corridor row 2-010 'Interface of Patient Data and Management Systems' (HH2-5A) covers the interface between patient data and management information systems — the EMR clinical data component. Row 2-009 'Fostering Internal Communication' covers internal communication standards. OP-SL-005 governs clinical communication systems broadly — EMR requirements, telephony, and secure messaging. PARTIAL because the EMR interface and internal communication rows structurally cover the clinical data and communication requirements, but the communication system governance framework (secure messaging protocols, telephony standards, clinical escalation paths) is an IT operational governance function extending beyond the Corridor's data interface and communication rows. Note: cross-domain overlap with IT-SA-001 (EHR System Management) — different governance layer (clinical communication requirements vs. IT system administration).

policyTitle: Service Delivery During Public Health Emergencies
summary: Defines clinical and operational protocols for maintaining services during public health emergencies including pandemic response.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Public health emergency response plan with pandemic-specific protocols
PPE stockpile documentation and replenishment records
Staff vaccination and health screening records during PHE
PHE service modification records (telehealth conversions, visit reductions)
justification: Corridor rows 1-011 'Emergency Management' and 1-012 'Disaster Planning' (HH1-8A family, 42 CFR §484.102) constitute the emergency management framework under which public health emergency protocols operate. OP-SL-006 governs clinical and operational protocols specific to public health emergencies — pandemic response, PPE management, clinical visit modifications, staff health screening. PARTIAL because 1-011 and 1-012 are the correct regulatory parents, but pandemic-specific clinical protocols (pathogen-specific PPE standards, cohorting practices, vaccination tracking, telehealth conversion protocols) substantially extend beyond the Corridor's general emergency management framework. Note: EMERGENCY_MANAGEMENT_SEMANTIC_CLUSTER with OP-FM-005 (parent) and OP-SL-007.

summary: Defines protocols for managing service delivery during inclement weather, natural disasters, and hazardous conditions.
realEvidenceArtifacts: Inclement weather response protocol with service suspension and alternative visit criteria
Staff safety assessment records for hazardous weather conditions
Patient notification records during weather-related service disruptions
Visit rescheduling and continuity records during adverse weather
justification: Corridor row 1-011 'Emergency Management' (HH1-8A, HH1-8A.01, 42 CFR §484.102) covers emergency preparedness including natural disasters and hazardous conditions as emergency management scenarios. OP-SL-007 governs the operational protocols for service delivery during inclement weather — visit suspension criteria, staff safety assessments, patient notification, and continuity measures. PARTIAL because 1-011 establishes the emergency management regulatory parent, but the operational protocols for inclement weather (visit-by-visit decision-making criteria, patient notification workflows, rescheduling management) are clinical operations procedures beyond the emergency management plan's governance scope. Note: EMERGENCY_MANAGEMENT_SEMANTIC_CLUSTER with OP-FM-005 (parent) and OP-SL-006.
